extracted.intended_audience: aspiring comedians, humor writers, performers, and people studying joke craft
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting and evaluating short jokes/punchlines that reliably produce laughs by using surprise, brevity, and recognizability. Targeted at people who write or perform jokes and want concrete criteria to improve funniness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise Inside a Frame of Recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: The audience must (a) be expecting one outcome and (b) recognize the alternative outcome the punchline reveals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pure surprise is just shock; pure recognition is just nodding. A good joke sets up a recognizable frame so the punchline's alternate outcome can be understood and appreciated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression
rubrics_metrics.description: Use as few words as possible — the fewer words a joke uses, the harder it hits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each unnecessary word delays the laugh and dilutes the surprise. The funniest jokes are the ones where you can't remove a single word; compress to the minimum that still preserves setup and punch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truth
rubrics_metrics.description: The best jokes feel true — they articulate something the audience already half-knew but had never put into words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The laugh is recognition of one's own thoughts being said out loud. Aim for observations or insights that ring true to your target audience rather than contrived cleverness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakes
rubrics_metrics.description: How much was the audience invested in the original expectation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A joke whose setup carries higher perceived importance or investment tends to produce a bigger payoff when subverted. Increasing stakes can amplify funniness, but must remain plausible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distance
rubrics_metrics.description: How far from the expectation does the punch travel?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Greater distance from the expected outcome can increase comedic impact, provided the new interpretation remains plausible in retrospect and recognizably tied to the setup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plausibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the new interpretation feel right in retrospect?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A punchline should make sense once revealed; retrospective plausibility makes the subversion satisfying rather than gratuitous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed
rubrics_metrics.description: How quickly does the audience get there?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Faster arrival at the intended reinterpretation increases comedic effect. Slow, meandering setups or delayed resolution reduce momentum and can weaken the laugh.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cleanness
rubrics_metrics.description: How few competing interpretations are there?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clean joke offers one clear alternate interpretation rather than several competing ones. Fewer possible readings reduce confusion and maximize the punch's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trying to be funny instead of being true (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Efforts that prioritize contrived humor over an honest observation or truth undermine funniness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid forcing jokes that don't arise from genuine insight; aim for truthfulness rather than artificial cleverness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explaining the joke (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Trying to explain the joke (e.g., 'get it?') kills the laugh.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you find yourself needing to explain, the joke likely failed to set the proper frame, compress cleanly, or establish plausibility. Leave the audience to connect the dots.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telegraphing the punch with your face (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Nonverbal cues that telegraph the punch before delivery reduce surprise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid facial or physical signals that let the audience predict the punch; preserve the element of surprise within the performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Using long, polysyllabic words (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overly long or complex words dilute speed and compression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer lean, conversational language. Polysyllabic or elevated diction can slow timing and make the joke feel labored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Making the audience the target (anti-pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Targeting the audience instead of the teller or the situation undermines rapport and can backfire.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Punching up at situations or oneself is safer and often funnier; attacking the audience risks alienation and reduces trustworthiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Did the audience hold a specific expectation?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the setup created a concrete expectation in the audience's mind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the necessary setup half of surprise; without a specific expectation, there is nothing meaningful for the punch to subvert.

rubrics_metrics.name: Did the punchline subvert it (not merely deflect it)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the punchline actively overturns the setup's expectation rather than diverting attention without meaningful contradiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subversion that reframes the setup is stronger than mere deflection or irrelevant distraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the new interpretation clean (one alternative, not three)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that the punchline proposes one clear alternate reading rather than multiple possible explanations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple interpretations exist, the audience may hesitate or split reactions; aim for a single clean reinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the joke compress to its minimum?
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether any words, beats, or qualifiers can be removed without losing the joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lean edits that preserve meaning increase impact. Over-explaining or padding weakens timing and surprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does the joke articulate a truth the audience knew but hadn't said?
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider whether the joke surfaces a shared, unspoken observation or insight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jokes that verbalize a communal recognition tend to produce stronger, more resonant laughs than purely absurd or random lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the joke trustworthy coming from the teller?
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the teller's persona, credibility, and rapport make the joke believable and acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trustworthiness affects whether an audience accepts a punchline (especially if it involves sensitive targets); a joke that feels incongruous with the teller can fall flat or offend.
